newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Philippines estimates rice, corn imports for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Philippines estimates rice, corn imports for 1997.

text.p: Philippine Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero III said on Wednesday the country's unmilled rice output in calendar 1997 will reach 12 million tonnes against estimated production of 11.52 million tonnes this year.

He told Reuters in an interview that production will still lag demand and projected rice imports at between 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes. Corn imports should also reach up to 500,000 tonnes, Escudero added.
"Rice production should reach about 12 million tonnes," Escudero said in an interview on the sidelines of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting in Singapore.
He said rice imports will probably be brought in by the end of the second quarter in 1997 and just ahead of the seasonally lean third quarter when supplies are normally tight.
Yellow corn imports will be necessary because of the Philippines' burgeoning poultry and livestocks industry.
"I cannot be conservative. I asked the President (Fidel Ramos) for a standby authority of 400,000 tonnes in corn imports," he said.
Shortages in rice and corn last year spiked inflation to a year high of more than 11.0 percent in September. Inflation stayed at double digits for more than six months.
